Entry.description:
One task in a blueprint: exactly one local key plus an ordinary manifest entry.

The flattened shape is intentional. An adopter who knows `aplan add --from` sees the same
fields at the same level. The typed embedding keeps the two surfaces from acquiring independent
field lists.

blocked_by.description:
Tasks this one waits on. May name a task the plan already has, or one any
entry in the same file declares an `id` for -- including a later one, so
a milestone can be written above the work it lists.

blocks.description:
Tasks which wait on this one. This reverse spelling is useful when a
creation batch needs to gate work that already exists; the target may
also be another explicitly-named entry in the same atomic manifest.

contains.description: Cuts or tasks whose work this checkpoint borrows for rollups.

cut.description: Milestone to join, by id or by the label the cut reports itself under.

effort.description:
Estimate in days. Refused when the entry is tagged `milestone`, because
a checkpoint carries no effort.

evidence.description:
Proof for a `done` ledger-correction entry. Refused on live entries and
resolved for the complete batch before any task or cut is written.

id.description:
Task id. Minted from the plan's convention when absent, exactly as
`aplan add` mints it.

key.description: The unique local name later entries use to refer to this task before it has a minted id.

paths.description:
Globs this task is responsible for. Refused when the entry is tagged
`milestone`, because a checkpoint owns no files.

phase.description: `phase`. Defaults to the cut's, then to the highest in use.

prefer_after.description:
Non-blocking ordering preferences. Like `blocked_by`, these may name an
id declared later in the same atomic manifest.

ratified_by.description: Independent review tasks that must be complete before this task closes.

revisit_at.description: RFC 3339 instant at which an initially parked task is worth reviewing.

status.description:
Initial lifecycle state. Ordinary creation accepts only live states;
`done` is reserved for the evidence-resolving ledger-correction path.
`dropped` is never a creation state because it records a later decision
not to do work that already existed.

title.description: Title, as a person would read it. The one required field.

traces.description: Document sections this task answers to.

version_impact_reason.description: Required explanation when an impact is below the task's level floor.

Evidence.description: A single piece of proof attached to a task.

captured.description:
ISO-8601 date the inline assertion was made. Required for `note`, because
an undated note is a rumour, and rejected on every machine-resolved kind:
an author-entered date is not freshness proof (`APLAN055`).

ref.description:
The pointer: a commit SHA, a URL, a repo-relative path, a test name, or
the note text itself.

EvidenceKind.description:
What kind of proof closes a task.

The point of typing this is that "I finished it" is not evidence. A commit,
a URL, a committed artefact, a named test, or a dated note is.

oneOf.description: A git commit SHA in this repository.
An external URL (a filing receipt, a regulator page, a vendor quote).
A repo-relative path to a committed artefact (a saved PDF, a transcript), optionally at a rev (`path@rev`) and optionally naming the section that proves it (`path#anchor`).
A named test that must pass.

A dated human note, the weakest kind. Use when nothing better exists,
e.g. the outcome of a phone call.

Parameter.description:
One declared string parameter.

Every V1 parameter is required. The language has no default key.

description.description: What value the author must supply and where the blueprint uses it.

name.description: The name used by placeholders such as `{{feature}}`.

Schema.description:
The language contract named by a document's `schema` key.

This is parser compatibility, not an author-controlled recipe revision. V1 has no revision or
provenance field because applying a blueprint is one-shot.

Status.description: Lifecycle of a task. `Done` is the only status that requires evidence.

oneOf.description: Not started. Eligible to be worked once its blockers clear.
Explicitly parked for a reason outside the dependency graph.
Complete. Requires at least one `evidence` entry.
Abandoned. Kept for the record rather than deleted.

VersionImpact.description:
What a change did to the thing that ships.

Ordered, and the order is the whole type: aggregation takes the strongest of
what a level floors and what its members claim, so `None < Fix < Feature <
Breaking` is what makes a `Breaking` task raise the cut above it.

It describes the **change**, and each scheme maps it to its own arithmetic:
semver at or past 1.0 sends `Breaking` to major, semver below 1.0 sends it to
minor, and `CalVer` takes its number from the calendar and keeps only the
compatibility claim.

oneOf.description: Changes nothing that ships. An operational log, a plan edit, or a note.
Something a consumer has to react to.

description.description: What the blueprint creates and when an author should use it.

name.description: A short human label for reports. It is not a catalog key or source identity.

parameters.description: Declared string parameters. Every declaration is required in V1.

schema.description: The language contract. Always `aplan/blueprint/v1`; it is not a recipe revision.

tasks.description: One or more ordinary task entries, each with a local key.

title.description: A human-readable title for the task shape this file creates.
